name: Ouroboros PD-2 'Aegis'
description:
A double-barreled derringer-format pistol chambered in .410/.45 Colt, capable of firing either shotshells or pistol rounds from its two over-under barrels. The Aegis provides maximum close-range versatility in a package small enough to conceal in an ankle holster — one barrel loaded with a .410 buckshot shell for close-range spread, one with a .45 Colt round for aimed fire. The operator selects which barrel fires first via a barrel-select switch on the frame.

Ouroboros designed the Aegis for people who want a backup weapon that can handle the two most common self-defense scenarios: an attacker at arm's reach (buckshot) and an attacker at room distance (pistol round). The double-barrel design means only two shots before reloading, but the combination of spread and precision in a pocket-sized package has made the Aegis the most popular backup weapon in GLMZ among security professionals and civilians alike.

The weapon's compact dimensions and dual-caliber capability have also made it popular in the Gray Zone, where .410 shotshells and .45 Colt rounds are among the most commonly available ammunition types. A Φ600 Aegis loaded with one buckshot shell and one .45 round provides a civilian with two different solutions to two different problems, in a weapon that disappears in an ankle holster and weighs less than a can of soda.
specifications: caliber: .410 bore / .45 Colt barrels: 2 (over-under) effective range: 5 meters (.410) / 15 meters (.45 Colt) weight: 0.3 kg length: 140mm barrel length: 75mm action: Double-action trigger with barrel select
tactical_use: Last-resort backup weapon and civilian self-defense. The Aegis provides two shots of mixed capability in the smallest possible package. Security professionals carry it as a backup to their primary weapon. Civilians carry it as their only weapon.
cultural_context: The Aegis has achieved cult status as GLMZ's 'everyone gun' — the weapon that shows up everywhere, from executive ankle holsters to the Gray Zone residents' coat pockets. Its versatility and compact size have made it the most common backup weapon in the city. 'Carrying an Aegis' is so common that it's become a metaphor for basic preparedness.
known_users: Corporate employees in lower-tier transit zones
story_hooks: An Aegis was used in a justified shooting that has become a cultural flashpoint — a Tier 1 resident shot a Tier 4 corporate employee in self-defense, and the subsequent legal proceedings have exposed the two-tier justice system that treats the same weapon differently depending on who carries it.

A gunsmith has discovered that a specific production run of Aegis derringers has barrels that are slightly out of alignment — the .410 barrel fires 3 degrees left of point of aim. At buckshot range it doesn't matter. At .45 Colt range, it means missing the target and hitting whatever is next to them. Ouroboros has not issued a recall.

physical_description.visual_profile: A stubby, business-end derringer with an unmistakably compact silhouette — barely larger than a closed fist. The over-under barrel arrangement creates a stacked, almost vertical presentation that reads as 'serious' despite its toy-like dimensions. Aesthetic sits between sleek minimalism and brutal pragmatism.
physical_description.dimensions: 140mm length, 65mm height, 28mm width. Twin 75mm barrels stacked vertically create a narrow profile optimized for ankle carry.
physical_description.weight_description: Featherweight in hand — 0.3kg feels almost insubstantial, like holding a dense pocket watch. This lightness belies the dual-caliber capability; perfect for long-term ankle carry without fatigue.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium-alloy frame with polymer grip panels. Barrel assembly uses hardened steel with DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents on the frame. The DLC-coated barrels have a dark graphite sheen that doesn't reflect light — tactical stealth aesthetic. Trigger guard and barrel selector lever feature polished stainless highlights.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, dark graphite barrels, brushed titanium frame edges, stainless steel controls. Minimal branding keeps the aesthetic understated.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with shallow diamond knurling — not aggressive, designed for secure control without sharp edges. Ergonomic contour fits the web of thumb and forefinger despite compact size.
distinctive_features: Dual barrel-select lever on left frame side — raised slightly, indexed for tactile identification in low-light
Double-action trigger with smooth, controlled break
Minimal iron sights (blade front, notch rear) molded into top strap
Recessed ejector rod with push-forward release for quick unloading
Frame-mounted safety lever positioned for thumb manipulation
Overstrike indicator pin visible from rear
Subtle stippling on grip panels for sweat resistance
Barrel address and caliber markings engraved on top strap in sans-serif typeface
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Ouroboros Solar Array Division logo — a stylized serpent consuming its tail — stamped on left grip panel. Serial number engraved on frame underside. Caliber/model designation (.410/.45 AEGIS) engraved on top strap between sights.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically well-maintained with light operational wear. Grip panels show minor scuffing from holster friction. Barrel selector lever may show patina from repeated use. No rust — DLC coating prevents corrosion even in wet conditions. Most civilian examples remain pristine; professional backup weapons show honest wear around muzzle and ejector rod.
